findings.reason: both nodes measure against the wrong quantity, so §1 would be built to a bound no correct fleet satisfies and §6 to a floor §1 forbids; the plan must name the lane's total worker capacity (or the router's width in workers) rather than its remaining headroom.
findings.text: §1's measure and deliverable cap live workers at "the router's published worker slots plus two", but the published `worker_slots` is "the extra workers the gate can carry" (reckon/crew/lane_document.py:484-485), i.e. headroom above the lane's current live runs, so the total live workers equal live runs plus that headroom and the guard fails on correct behaviour whenever the lane carries more than two live runs — the same figure makes §6's "at least 175 live worker processes" (:74) against a router of width 80 unreachable on the §1 fixed code

findings.reason: without a control that drives the count under 175 (a half-width window, or a deliberate cap), the clause is an assertion the record can only pass, and it is the clause the previous round introduced to replace the stand-in's self-reported median.
findings.text: the clause added by the last revision, "a count of live worker processes across the nodes of at least 175 at every reading", is falsified by no named control: the only control fires at a revision before §1 lands, where a base behaviour that starts the harness early makes the process count higher, so the base arm cannot show this lower bound ever refuses, and no reading in the plan is required to come out below 175

findings.reason: the tolerance is undelimitable against the endpoint it guards; it needs a derivation from the per-worker budget at target scale, otherwise §2 can be closed on a memory figure that grows with worker count.
findings.text: §2 allows the server's median resident memory at 40 workers to sit 0.5 GB above its median at 5, while the plan's own table (:38) records that same server at "0.42 GB mean" — so the guard tolerates growth larger than the server's entire mean footprint and cannot distinguish "does not grow with the number of workers it serves" from a leak of about 13 MB per worker, which is roughly 2.2 GB at the 175 workers §6 requires

findings.reason: the followup is the instruction the coordinator reads when it queues the batch, so the §6 node would be gated on four of its five declared upstreams and could start before the MCP-set work §3 lands.
findings.text: the s6 depends-on declaration (:22) and §6's deliverable (:73) now name sections 1 to 5, but the followup that drives the dispatch still says "§6 is the scale rehearsal and waits on §1, §2, §4 and §5", omitting §3

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the dependency work-flows-to-the-lane#s71 resolves (docs/plans/work-flows-to-the-lane.html:344), plan-after work-flows-to-the-lane resolves, and the cited evidence fragment paths are the deliverables themselves.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §6's new "at least 175 live worker processes at every reading" clause carries no control that can falsify it (docs/plans/work-scales-to-eighty-across-nodes.html:74), and §2's 0.5 GB allowance exceeds the whole mean footprint the plan records for that server (:54).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every section logs to docs/evidence/fragments/work-scales-to-eighty-across-nodes/s1..s6.html in the repository, no session scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no section names a symbol, file or function, and no plan label, stage name or ticket number appears in the plan's own vocabulary.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §1 bounds live workers against "the router's published worker slots" (docs/plans/work-scales-to-eighty-across-nodes.html:49), a figure the repository defines as the gate's remaining headroom rather than the lane's total capacity, so the figure is the wrong quantity for both §1's bound and §6's floor.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §1 delivers a queued request holding no process (its base census is evidence for that one goal), §2 one server per node, §3 a declared MCP set, §6 the lane held at 80.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the followup f-wse-001 at docs/plans/work-scales-to-eighty-across-nodes.html:82 still has §6 waiting on §1, §2, §4 and §5, while the s6 depends-on declaration names all five sections.
